title: Squirrels in Central Park
text:
Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
squirrel_data <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2023/2023-05-23/squirrel_data.csv')
view(squirrel_data)




Code
squirrel_data <- squirrel_data |> 
  filter(Age %in% c("Adult", "Juvenile"))




Code
ggplot(squirrel_data, aes(x = X, y = Y, color = Age))+
  geom_point(
    size = 1,
    alpha = 0.3)+
  labs(
    x = "Longtitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    title = "Adults and Juvenile Squirrels Sighted in Central Park")

title: Squirrels in Central Park
text:
Data Source: Data Science Learning Community. (2023). Tidy Tuesday: 2023-05-23. TidyTuesday. GitHub
Original data source: NYC Open Data. (2018). 2018 Central Park Squirrel Census – Squirrel Data. City of New York. NYC Open Data
The scatterplot illustrates the location squirrels were spotted in Central Park. They were mostly adults squirrels with a few juveniles. One thing to note on the graph is the empty space in the middle of the park, which is the where the lake is located, hence, no squirrels were spotted.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

Code

Code

    size = 1,

  labs(
    x = "Longtitude",
    y = "Latitude",
    title = "Adults and Juvenile Squirrels Sighted in Central Park")

title: Spotify Songs
text:
Data Source: Data Science Learning Community. (2020). Tidy Tuesday: 2020-01-21. TidyTuesday. GitHub
Original data source / spotifyr: Thompson, C., Parry, J., Phipps, D., & Wolff, T. (2020). spotifyr: R wrapper for the Spotify Web API. spotifyr
The boxplot shows the popularity rating of different genre on Spotify. Pop music followed by latin music have popularities just over 50, while EDM has the lowest popularity.


Code
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)
spotify_songs <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-01-21/spotify_songs.csv')
view(spotify_songs)




Code
ggplot(
  spotify_songs, 
  aes(
    x = reorder(playlist_genre, track_popularity, FUN = median),
    y = track_popularity))+
    geom_boxplot()+
    labs(x = "Playlist genre",
    y = "Popularity",
    title = "Popularity by playlist genre")
